Connector contract tests

Source: R/connector_contract_tests.R
connector_contract_tests.Rd

A shared set of testthat tests for the behaviour every connector backend should share, as described in vignette("Consistent-API"): what each method returns, that data read back equals data written, and that listing reflects writes and removals.

Usage

connector_contract_tests(cases = connector_contract_cases())

connector_contract_cases(
  name = "contract.rds",
  data = data.frame(x = c(1, 2, 3), y = c("a", "b", "c")),
  expect_read_back = function(object, expected) {
     testthat::expect_equal(object,
    expected, label = "read_cnt(cnt, name) return value", expected.label =
    "the written data")
 }
)

Arguments

cases

Cases to start the suite with, as a named list of named lists of function(cnt), grouped by method. Pass connector_contract_cases(...) to change the default test data, or list() to start empty.

name

Name used to write the test data. Its extension, if any, decides the file format. The default .rds reads back exactly what was written.

data

Any R object the backend can write under name with write_cnt().

expect_read_back

A testthat expectation, function(object, expected), used by the read_cnt() read-back case. object is what read_cnt() returned and expected is data. It must call testthat::expect_*() functions. The default expects them to be equal, which suits formats that keep the object as written, such as .rds. Pass your own for backends that don't, e.g. a database that returns rows in any order.

Value

connector_contract_tests(): a ConnectorContract object.

connector_contract_cases(): a named list of named lists of functions.

Details

connector_contract_tests() returns a ConnectorContract suite, by default with the cases from connector_contract_cases(): a named list with one entry per connector method, each a named list of cases. A case is a function(cnt) that runs expectations against a new, empty connector. Print the suite to see what will run, and change it before running it:

  • drop a method the backend does not support: suite$remove_method("create_directory_cnt")

  • drop a case: suite$remove_case("read_cnt", "errors on missing content")

  • add a case: suite$add_case("read_cnt", "<case>", function(cnt) ...)

The builder methods change the suite in place and return it, so they chain. Use suite$clone() to change a copy instead.

Case names describe the expected behaviour of their method, and are unique within it. The same name can describe several methods, e.g. "returns the connector". suite$run() runs every case as its own testthat::test_that(), named "connector contract: <method>() <case>". Call it from a test file in a package that extends connector.

Debugging a failing case

Failures name the case and say what was expected, but point at the line that calls suite$run(), not at the case itself. A case is a plain function, so you can print its code and step through it:

case <- connector_contract_tests()$get_case(
  "remove_cnt",
  "returns the connector and removes content"
)
case                                     # prints the case's code
cnt <- new_connector(env = globalenv())  # your connector function
debugonce(case)
case(cnt)

Examples

connector_contract_tests()
#> <ConnectorContract> with 10 cases
#> `write_cnt()`
#> • returns the connector
#> `read_cnt()`
#> • returns the written data
#> • errors on missing content
#> `list_content_cnt()`
#> • lists written content
#> `remove_cnt()`
#> • returns the connector and removes content
#> `create_directory_cnt()`
#> • with open = FALSE returns the connector
#> • with open = TRUE returns a new connector
#> `remove_directory_cnt()`
#> • returns the connector and removes it
#> `download_cnt()`
#> • returns the connector and creates a file
#> `upload_cnt()`
#> • returns the connector and adds content

# tests/testthat/test-contract.R
connector_contract_tests()$
  remove_method("download_cnt")$
  remove_method("upload_cnt")$
  run(new_connector = \(env) {
    connector_fs(withr::local_tempdir(.local_envir = env))
  })
#> ✔ | F W  S  OK | Context
#> 
#> ⠏ |          0 | connector contract                                             
#> ⠋ |          1 | connector contract                                             
#> ⠴ |          6 | connector contract                                             
#> ✔ |         13 | connector contract
#> 
#> ══ Results ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#> [ FAIL 0 | WARN 0 | SKIP 0 | PASS 13 ]
